subject: POC trial: model selection + success criteria (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 16:14:00 -0800
Subject: Recap & next steps — Acme POC (model selection + success criteria)

Hi Sophie —

Great to chat today. Thanks for walking us through the clinical triage use case and the sample prompts. Per our discussion, I summarized the proposed POC plan below so we have alignment on success criteria, timelines, owners, and the recommended model candidates for the trial.

High-level objective:
- Evaluate a 4-week POC to validate that Redwood inference can meet your clinical triage quality and latency targets while keeping per-call cost within your budget.

Proposed success criteria (pass/fail style):
1) Quality: clinical triage accuracy >= 88% on validated holdout set of 1,000 cases (we will define exact label schema).
2) Safety/hallucination: < 2% clinically actionable hallucinations on sample prompts and adversarial set.
3) Latency: p95 single-turn response < 350ms (US region) for average prompt length (~150 tokens).
4) Cost: expected cost <= $0.09 per inference (token-based estimate) for the evaluated model/config.
5) Integration: Redwood SDK integration completed and end-to-end pipeline demoable by week 4.

POC timeline (6-week plan, but core eval is 4 weeks):
- Week 0 (this week): Kickoff, access, sample prompts & labels delivered by Acme.
- Week 1: Infrastructure setup, data ingestion, baseline runs (out-of-the-box prompts).
- Week 2: Model A baseline evaluation + metric collection.
- Week 3: Model B baseline + quick tuning, run safety scans and multilingual checks.
- Week 4: Integration testing, latency tuning, final evaluation, and review.
- Week 5-6: If needed, iterate on prompts and small instruction tuning or reranking.

Model candidates (recommended for trial):
- Primary candidate: Llama-2-13B-chat (instruction-tuned). Strong middle-ground for instruction-following and cost.
- Fallback / low-cost candidate: Mistral-7B-Instruct (4-bit quantized) — good latency and lower cost for high-throughput scenarios.
- Optional high-capacity candidate (if you want to test higher quality): Falcon-40B-instruct (will increase cost and latency; we can run a small sample).

Multilingual considerations:
- You mentioned triage notes in English + Spanish and occasional French. We'll run multilingual benchmarks: Llama-2-13B performs okay for Spanish; if we see gaps, we recommend either translation pre/post process or considering a model variant tuned for multilingual (we'll surface results).

Owners / contacts:
- Redwood PM / sales: Marissa Cole (me) — program lead and success criteria owner.
- Redwood infra / model ops: Aditya Rao — will run baselines, quantization, and latency tuning.
- Redwood SDK / integration: Dev Patel — leads integration and sample app.
- Acme lead: Sophie Martin — dataset and label contact.

Deliverables we need from Acme this week:
- Representative sample prompts + anonymized labels (CSV preferred).
- List of top 50 edge-case prompts you want us to prioritize for hallucination testing.

Attachments: POC-success-criteria.docx (detailed checklist), sample_prompts.csv (sample format).

Next step: Sophie — can you confirm dataset ETA (mentioned Tues next week) and that we can start infra access? If yes, we'll schedule the kickoff on Monday.

Thanks —
Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — Acme POC (model selection + success criteria)

Thanks Marissa — this looks good. Quick confirmations from our side: 

- Dataset ETA: We can deliver the anonymized sample prompts + labels by Tuesday 3/2 end of day.
- Top 50 edge cases: We'll share these in the same CSV (column flag).
- Multilingual: Spanish is ~25% of workflows, French ~5%. If you can include language labels in the CSV that would help.

On success criteria, the clinical team is comfortable with the accuracy target you proposed but wants us to pay special attention to hallucination definitions (we'll provide examples). Latency target is aggressive but worthwhile — happy to see the baseline.

We approve starting infra access next week. Please send the access instructions and a calendar invite for kickoff (Mon 3/1 or Tue 3/2 morning PST).

Sophie
Head of Clinical AI, Acme Health

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — Acme POC (model selection + success criteria)

Hi Sophie / team —

Thanks for confirming. A few technical notes on model selection and what we'll run during the baseline week: 

1) Baseline config:
- Llama-2-13B-chat (float16) on single A100/GPU for quality baselines. We'll capture token-level latency and cost estimates.
- Mistral-7B-Instruct (4-bit quantized) on triton-backed nodes for a lower-cost baseline and throughput tests.
- Falcon-40B sample (2-3 cases) if you want a quick sense of marginal quality lift.

2) Evaluation plan / metrics:
- Quality: classification-style accuracy on your labeled holdout + macro F1 for multi-class triage decisions.
- Safety: automated hallucination detector + manual review for flagged cases.
- Latency: measure p50/p95 for single-turn and per-token streaming throughput.
- Cost: runtime token cost estimate + per-call cost for average prompt.
- Multilingual: stratified metrics (EN/ES/FR) and failure mode analysis per language.

3) Fallback routing approach:
- If L2-13B meets quality and latency targets, use it as primary.
- Otherwise, use a fallback policy: short prompts -> Mistral-7B for cost-sensitive high-throughput; long/context prompts -> L2-13B. Redwood can set routing policies for the trial.

4) Quick wins we can do during week 2-33:
- KV prefix caching for repeated patient-context prompts (should cut per-token cost for multi-turn flows).
- Aggressive batching for background batch scoring (non-interactive).

I'll provision a small sandbox in the Redwood console and share credentials + a step-by-step integration guide by EOD today. Dev, can you confirm the sample app repo branch and we'll post the invite for kickoff?

—Aditya
Sr. Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference

1) Please include an expected data handling / retention statement for the sandbox (we need to confirm with security).
2) If you have quick cost estimates for L2-13B vs Mistral-7B for the planned workload (50k calls/month), please share in the kickoff doc.

We look forward to the sandbox access.

Sophie
